articles.title: Gronk Says 49ers Beat Themselves More Than Falcons Won
articles.summary: Rob Gronkowski breaks down the 49ers loss to Atlanta, citing years of injury struggles and self-inflicted errors that cost the game on Sunday.
articles.body:
Rob Gronkowski believes the San Francisco 49ers lost to the Atlanta Falcons because they failed themselves, not because Atlanta played a perfect game. The former tight end pointed to a long history of injuries plaguing the 49ers roster before Sunday's 29-20 loss at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. He argues that the team's magic will return once healthy players like Mike Evans come back after the bye week.

The 49ers dropped their first game of the season on Sunday, October 25. They now sit at 6-1 overall but face a critical injury list. According to Heavy.com , Gronkowski voiced serious worry regarding the injury bug still affecting the squad. He remains a firm believer that these issues will not affect the team in the long run.

Gronkowski asked a blunt question during his podcast. "Why are the 49ers always injured? We're not even talking about this year, not last year, I'm talking about the last 4-5 years. Why are they always injured?" He noted that many guys are on injured reserve but designated to return. The panic meter for the San Francisco 49ers is not going off according to him.

On Monday, roughly 24 hours following the defeat, head coach Kyle Shanahan addressed the media. Shanahan disclosed that seven players stand a strong likelihood of returning after the bye week. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson are among those included in that group. Nick Bosa, the star pass rusher, is expected to return after missing the last few weeks.

The core of the loss was not a lack of talent from Atlanta. Gronkowski further stated that magic will diminish somewhat if weapons around you are absent. He thinks the magic will return immediately once Mike Evans and company resume play after the bye week. His final take on the game was sharp and direct.

"The 49ers beat themselves more than the Atlanta Falcons won this game." This statement cuts through the noise of the final score. Brock Purdy, who is currently playing at an MVP level, functions as a huddle extension of Kyle Shanahan per Gronk. The system works when the personnel is healthy. The Falcons just capitalized on the mistakes San Francisco made.

The Falcons are now 4 spots higher in power rankings according to reports. They sit at No. 21 after the upset win. This team faces its true challenge on the defensive side. Jeff Ulbrich's unit sits fourth against the run yet ranks only 29th against the pass. Converting high pressure numbers into sacks is the key to the next game.

In Week 9, James Pearce will become eligible to return from suspension which will help the pass rush. The Falcons must keep Penix upright to beat them. The 49ers loss proves that even the best teams can fall if they hurt themselves first.

articles.title: Trey Nyoni On Liverpool Chances as Iraola Embraces Youth and Rotation
articles.summary: The 19-year-old midfielder is on pace to play between 1,500 and 2,000 first team minutes this eason.
articles.body:
With Liverpool heading into the 2026-27 season without making any signings to address their depth issues in midfield, the chances were always high that 19-year-old academy graduate Trey Nyoni would be given chances to show what he could do by new head coach Andoni Iraola.

It might even be fair to say Liverpool's hopes for the season reseted in part on Nyoni being able to take those chances when they did come.

To his credit, and rather fortunately for the team, he's done just that. The youngster has made nine appearances to date, seeing the pitch in 75% of the games played in all competitions and earning 373 minutes—numbers which would project to 1,500-2,000 minutes across the entire season.

"My motive has always just been,whet her I'm on the pitch for a minute, five minutes, 10 minutes, 90 minutes, I just try to make the most out of the minutes I get," Nyoni said ahead of Wednesday's League Cup tie against Chelsea, which he is widely expected to start.

"But I think in the last few weeks obviously I've had a lot of exposure, which has been good for me. It's something different, playing a lot of minutes within a short space of tim, but it has been really good."

He's not the only youngster seeing big minutes early as Iraola looks to navigate a season where the Red will be trying to go deep and compete for silverware in four competitions despite a squad largely seen as thin at multiple positions and not just in midfield, with Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas also seeing plenty of action.

"For me it's positive to see the younger players," Nyoni added. "Obviously we need to stick together, help each other as much as possible. We know that being here, it's not easy, there's a lot of world-class players here. They're going to push us every day.

"I think having that allows us to keep pushing on and keep progressing. Every time we go on the pitch, I think none of us are really nervous—I think we all go out there and give 100%. That's what's important."

articles.title: Fenerbahçe coach quits a month after previous resignation
articles.summary: Fenerbahçe coach Ismail Kartal has resigned less than 24 hours after the Istanbul derby defeat against Galatasaray. "After talks with our club leadership, th...
articles.body:
Fenerbahçe coach Ismail Kartal has resigned less than 24 hours after the Istanbul derby defeat against Galatasaray.

"After talks with our club leadership, this decision was accepted by mutual agreement and with mutual recognition and appreciation," Fenerbahçe said in a statement on Tuesday after the 2-1 league defeat. Fener are fifth, six points behind leaders Galatasaray.

In September, Kartal also offered his resignation but Fenerbahçe president Aziz Yildirim rejected it.

According to Yildirim, Kartal was then upset by a fan throwing a bottle at his head.

His fourth spell as coach at Fener ends after only a few months. He had previously managed the club in 2014-2015, 2022 and 2023-2024.

The derby between arch-rivals Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe on Monday was overshadowed by a fracas after the final whistle. Players from both teams went at each other on the pitch. Police and security forces had to intervene.

articles.title: Arsenal cup match at Fleetwood Town paused due to drone
articles.summary: A flying object caused a stoppage of just less than 10 minutes during the Gunners' visit to Fleetwood Town.
articles.body:
Arsenal's Carabao Cup match with Fleetwood Town was only two minutes old when referee Michael Salisbury stopped the match because of a drone hovering above the field.

The delay lasted less than 10 minutes as Salisbury spoke with both teams' coaching staffs, police and organizers at the intimate Highbury Stadium in northwest England.

Both teams kept warm for five minutes by staying on the field and passing a ball around before the referee called over the captains in the 8th minute and explained why he was pulling the teams off the field.

The source of the drone looked to be identified, and play resumed in the 10th minute with a free kick where an Arsenal player had been fouled eight minutes earlier.

Even before the stoppage, there were some confusing moments at the start of the game. Fleetwood Town play in red shirts with white sleeves and at a venue called Highbury, matching Arsenal's typical kit and the name of their former venue.

Fleetwood Town's Highbury, however, holds just 5,327 fans, with around 2,600 of those seated. The League Two club scored the opener thanks to 20-year-old Aaron Loupalo-Bi.

articles.title: Former Washington Nationals GM Mike Rizzo getting interviewed by the Astros
articles.summary: The long time Nationals GM is interviewing with the club he beat in the 2019 World Series
articles.body:
When he was fired in July of 2025, I was curious to see what was next for Mike Rizzo. At the time, he was 64 years old, but he did not seem to have any desire to step away. After a year on the sidelines, Rizzo is in the mix for the Astros GM job. Yesterday, Bob Nightengale reported that Rizzo would get an interview.

We will see if he gets the job, but I would sure be curious to see how he would do in Houston. The Nats and Astros also have quite a few connections. Obviously, Houston was the team that Mike Rizzo's Nats beat in the 2019 World Series. The two clubs also share a Spring Training site at West Palm Beach.

If Rizzo gets hired, we will be seeing a lot of him during Spring Training. It would be very interesting to contrast how the two teams do things at the same Spring Training site. Rizzo's successor in DC, Paul Toboni, has changed a lot since he took over. The "I don't care how hard you throw ball four" signs have been replaced by Traject Machines and other tech.

Despite Rizzo being an old school guy, I do not think it would be impossible for him to have success in Houston. He would have to adapt some, but a veteran Astros team that is not afraid to spend money would suit Rizzo better than a young, smaller budget club.

Rizzo may not be an innovator at this stage of his career, he still has an eye for a good trade and does a solid job with pro scouting. I still believe that he will have to lean into analytics more than he did, but maybe he has learned some lessons since being let go in DC. That is definitely something that will be brought up in his interview which is taking place today.

Based on his past achievements, Rizzo would be a strong candidate. He turned the Nats into one of the best teams in baseball last decade. However, the 2020's have been a different story for Rizzo. Bad drafting and an inability to adapt led to him losing his edge.

How much of this was his fault and how much was he hamstrung by the Lerner's? If he gets the Astros job, we will be able to find out. He built a World Series championship team and won the NL East four times, but there is not a ton of recent success here.

It is also no lock that Rizzo gets the job either. He is one of several candidates in the Astros search. However, the interest he is getting for this job seems to be more serious than when he was floated as a candidate for the A's gig.

If Rizzo gets the job, I will be rooting for him. Things did not end well in DC, but I appreciate the good times as well. For Astros fans sake, I hope you are getting 2010's Rizzo and not the 2020's version.

articles.title: Deion Sanders says offer of $50,000 to critics was "a joke"
articles.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders has addressed the comments made recently by Christopher "Uncle" Neely regarding a supposed willingness to pay critics $50,000 to...
articles.body:
Colorado coach Deion Sanders has addressed the comments made recently by Christopher "Uncle" Neely regarding a supposed willingness to pay critics $50,000 to not mention his name.

At a press conference on Tuesday, Sanders said it was " a joke ."

"I think you misinterpreted that," Sanders said. "I said . . . I would love to give you money and not mention my name, and I want to see how far that goes. That was a joke, That's what we were saying. Like some people live on your name."

Before Sanders answered, someone off camera (presumably Neely) can be heard explaining the question. The person refers to a show from the spring in which that statement was made.

Sanders did indeed previously make a comment along those lines. And it does indeed sound like a hypothetical, not an actual offer.

Separately, Deion posted the following on Twitter this afternoon: " This is a lie but God bless u all. Y'all know me and have known me for years. When has it appeared that I've EVER cared what a man or woman has said about me? My son does my Videos and Neely is a friend."

While it does appear that Sanders was not making a real offer when he talked about it previously, that's not how Neely's recent comments came off: "For the most part, the people that attack him wouldn't be making the money they were making if he wasn't here to attack. Which is why he told some of them , 'Hey man, let's just do this. I give you $50,000 to not mention my name for a year.' And ain't nobody took the deal yet. . . . And you love talking about this man so much, and you make so much talking of this man that you turned the deal down."

To answer the question Deion posed on Twitter ("When has it appeared that I've EVER cared what a man or woman has said about me?"), there is at least one tangible example of sensitivity to criticism. In 2024, for example, he refused to answer a question at a press conference from a reporter at the local CBS affiliate because of a problem he had with CBS generally.

" I'm not doing anything with CBS ," Sanders said at the time. "Next question. . . . It ain't got nothing to do with you. It's above that. It ain't got nothing to do with you. I've got love for you. I appreciate and respect you. It ain't got nothing to do with you. They know what they did."

"I'm here in Denver not national," the reporter responded.

"You are who you are," Deion replied. "CBS is CBS, all right? . . . I'm looking you in the eye as a man. I respect you. I've got love for you. But what they did was foul."

Regardless, Neely stated the offer — and the failure of any reporters to accept it — as if it were a real offer. Sanders has now given his side of the story that Neely created with the content and tone of his recent remarks.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni defended decision to play Saquon Barkley after RB suffered another injury
articles.summary: It hasn't been a great couple weeks on the injury front for the Eagles.
articles.body:
The past couple weeks haven't exactly been a banner display for the Eagles on the injury front . And on Monday, head coach Nick Sirianni once again found himself answering for the decisions of his medical team.

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley had missed the past two weeks with a hamstring injury and was listed as questionable heading into Monday night's game against the Cowboys. But after just seven carries and two receptions, Barkley exited the game and didn't return.

Though Barkley left with an announced back injury, Sirianni was still asked if he felt the Eagles rushed the star running back to return.

He defended how the Eagles handled the injury to reporters after the game. Via Pro Football Talk :

"Obviously, you saw that he was on a pitch count out there today. There was constant communication to see how he was feeling, see where he was, and obviously, he came out early in the second half. Again, when you go into something like that, you make sure that the player's health is first and foremost. Is he ready to go? Do they feel ready to go? Do the doctors and trainers feel like they're ready to go? We felt like that was the case today, but obviously wanted to keep a close eye on him, and he's tough as heck. He wanted to be out there for his teammates, probably had to slow him [down] as far as -- he'd be out there every play because of the person he is and the teammate he is and the player he is and the toughness that he has. "So, we tried to be smart with him there, but it was good to have him back out there. He obviously had a nice game and was very productive when he touched the football."

articles.title: Jaren Jackson Jr. out six weeks with MCL tear, Lauri Markkanen day-to-day with wrist sprain
articles.summary: SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — Jazz forward Jaren Jackson Jr. will be sidelined for at least six weeks after tearing the MCL in his right knee during the second quart...
articles.body:
SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — Jazz forward Jaren Jackson Jr. will be sidelined for at least six weeks after tearing the MCL in his right knee during the second quarter of Utah's 110-105 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies .

Lauri Markkanen, who sprained his right wrist in the first quarter of the same game on Monday night, is listed as day to day.

Jackson and Markkanen were two of the top three scorers for the Jazz in the team's first three games.

Both players have struggled with injuries during their time in Utah.

Markkanen appeared in only 89 games over his previous two seasons with the Jazz and has not appeared in more than 66 games in a season since being traded to Utah before the 2022-23 season.

Jackson only appeared in three games with Utah last season after being acquired in a trade with Memphis before undergoing season-ending surgery on his left knee.

articles.title: Hail State star QB Kamario Taylor to miss Longhorns game, season
articles.summary: The Longhorns will not face Kamario Taylor on Saturday. The star Mississippi State QB has been ruled out for the rest of the season.
articles.body:
One of college football's breakout stars is out for the season and will miss Saturday's clash in Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns . Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor will miss the rest of the season after it was announced he'd need surgery on his injured toe.

Taylor injured his toe on Sept. 26 against Missouri. He has tried to play in two games since, against Alabama on Oct. 3 and Oklahoma this past Saturday. In both efforts, the Macon, MS product didn't look anywhere close to 100% and left both games early. In fact, it looked like he made it worse against the Sooners.

The true sophomore entered the national spotlight after leading Hail State to a 4-0 record. The Bulldogs have struggled to win any games over the past few seasons. Taylor was under center for wins against Minnesota and South Carolina on the road and No. 19 Missouri at home.

Taylor's season ends with 17 passing touchdowns, 1,460 passing yards and a 65% completion percentage. At 6-foot-4 and 230 pounds, he is physically a lot like Vince Young and is already one of the country's most dominant and dangerous players.

As the Maryland football team fired head coach Mike Locksley after another disappointing season, the program is making efforts to find the next best option for the school. While rumors surround the Maryland football team regarding the next head coach, the latest development details the next step in finding the next head coach.

According to college football insider Pete Nakos of On3 Sports, the Terrapins have hired "search firm ZRG Turnkey" to help with the search for the school's future head coach after Locksley.

"Maryland has hired search firm ZRG Turnkey to assist with its head football coaching search, sources tell [On3]," Nakos wrote Tuesday on X, formerly Twitter.

Athletic director Jim Smith spoke about the decision, saying that the school "will get a really good coach," according to The Baltimore Sun.

"I was fortunate enough to [have] the bye week," Smith said. "So there wasn't the immediate urgency. There aren't also a lot of bye week changes. As you saw this week, there were two coaches let go, and it was immediate. So I had a little bit more time. I wanted to make sure I was not making an emotional decision, and we came to the right conclusion for the program when we announced on Wednesday."

The news of Maryland football firing Mike Locksley was a "stunner"

When it comes to the players' reactions to the news, outside linebacker Sidney Stewart would be honest in saying how much of a "stunner" it was to see Locksley fired.

"For it to actually happen, it definitely was a stunner for me and the rest of the team," Stewart said. "I have a lot of love for him. I really appreciate him. He's impacted me on and off the field. But ultimately, I know that the people that are still here and are part of this program made the right choice…so I'm just riding the ship."

Locksley has coached the Terrapins since 2019, amassing a 39-54 record with the program. With Aazaar Abdul-Rahim as the interim head coach, he'll look to lead Maryland (2-5) on Saturday against Illinois, hoping to snap the five-game skid.

articles.title: Brewers payroll breakdown: How Milwaukee built World Series contender on a small-ball budget
articles.summary: The Brewers have defied the odds by reaching the precipice of a championship. Here's how they did it.
articles.body:
The numbers don't lie: there is a correlation between payroll and winning in MLB, but it's far from an exact science.

The Brewers have defied the odds in 2026, taking baseball's 19th-ranked payroll and winning 103 games before cruising to the doorstep of a championship. Even the 2015 Royals, often propped up as the most recent example of a team with a reduced payroll winning the World Series, ranked in the top half among all teams.

How is it possible? The Brewers left no stone unturned to find quality players, from David Stearns' tenure atop the front office to Matt Arnold's four years at the helm.

Here's a look at how Milwaukee built a World Series roster with a lower payroll than more than half of the league.

The Brewers rank 19th in baseball with a $146.2 million payroll, behind a group of 18 teams that includes the 62-100 Angels, 65-97 Giants and 69-93 Royals.

Even more impressive is the fact that most of Milwaukee's highest-paid players weren't the biggest contributors to the team's success this season. Christian Yelich regressed, Brandon Woodruff missed most of the year with shoulder trouble, and trade deadline additions Dustin May and Antonio Senzatela have been complementary pieces at best.

So, how did the Brewers build a roster capable of winning the World Series? Here are all of the key moves.

Of the 26 players on the Brewers' World Series roster, here is the breakdown:

Of the four players signed by the Brewers as free agents, only one was an actual major-league free agent. The remaining three were teenage international free agents. More than half of the roster, meanwhile, was brought in through trades.

Here's a full look at the roster and method of acquisition.

Eight Brewers draft picks are on the World Series roster, including five drafted outside the first round. Jacob Misiorowski and Aaron Ashby were both small-school draft picks, while Cooper Pratt became a top-100 prospect despite falling all the way to the sixth round.

Jackson Chourio, Abner Uribe and Luis Lara were all international free-agent signings, so Sanchez, at just $1.75 million, is the only major-league free-agent signing on the Brewers' roster.

More than half of the Brewers' roster was acquired through trade. Kyle Harrison, David Hamilton and Shane Drohan have all played smaller roles in the postseason, but they came over in February's Caleb Durbin trade, while Joey Ortiz and DL Hall were acquired in the 2024 Corbin Burnes deal. Robert Gasser was also brought in as part of a larger trade, as he was part of the return for Josh Hader in 2022.

William Contreras was tossed into the three-team Sean Murphy trade with the Braves and Athletics but quickly proved to be a steal for the Brewers, while Jake Bauers and Trevor Megill were acquired in minor deals — Megill was dealt for a player to be named later — but have become critical pieces in Milwaukee.

articles.title: Dream coach Karl Smesko calls WNBA Finals officiating ‘just ridiculous’ as Angel Reese also questions refs
articles.summary: Angel Reese and coach Karl Smesko blasted WNBA Finals officiating after the Atlanta Dream's Game 5 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in the series.
articles.body: Dream head coach Karl Smesko came to Angel Reese’s defense after the Atlanta dropped Game 5 of the WNBA Finals. Smesko argued officials missed what he considered a "ridiculous" amount of contact against Atlanta's star forward and the league's reigning Defensive Player of the Year. "I give [the Valkyries] credit for playing good defense, they're known for their defense," Smesko said. "But I want to have Angel's back here. The contact on Angel compared to everybody else is just ridiculous. Just ridiculous," Smesko said after the 64-55 loss Monday to the Golden State Valkyries. Reese finished Game 5 with seven points as the loss pushed the Dream to the brink of elimination. Although she seemed to struggled offensively, Reese still pulled down 15 rebounds. The series now shifts back to Atlanta on Thursday for Game 6. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Smesko added a blunt assessment of the officiating in the WNBA Finals: "You can't be at this level and make that many mistakes." Smesko’s primary frustration centered on what he believed were several missed calls involving Reese. He also pointed to possible missed double-dribble and traveling violations by the Valkyries. Reese echoed her coach’s sentiments, suggesting this series was not the first time she contended with physical play and questionable officiating this year. "I am still trying to figure out how to play through the physicality," said Reese, who was also called for four personal fouls. "I'm kind of used to it because this was happening throughout the season, so I have to just continue to play through it. But honestly, for my teammates, when they're getting slapped to the floor or knocked off, it's a little frustrating." The three-time All-Star continued: "I know I have the mismatch, especially talking about matchups. So when I do switch on the post and I'm a lot stronger than the opponent, I should be able to turn and they're calling an offensive foul. But when I'm getting pushed before that, it's frustrating to me." WNBA FINALS GAME 6, A POTENTIAL TITLE-CLINCHER, WILL BE HELD IN THE AFTERNOON ON THURSDAY Reese was also held to single-digit scoring in Game 4, finishing the 67-62 loss with eight points. Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase argued the physical nature of Game 5 was to be expected this late in a championship series. "Both teams really want to win this," Nakase said. "These are two defensive-minded teams ... they like physicality, so that's part of it. I ain't shocked about this. You have an Atlanta Dream team that's well-coached, that have dogs, same as us." As a team, the Dream attempted 14 free throws in Game 5, their fewest in a playoff game this postseason. Reese pointed to a shift in the way officials have called games as the series has gone on. "It definitely shifted when we went up 2-1," Reese said. "I don't know what happened, but it definitely took a big turn." Game 5 was defined by defense, with both the Dream and Valkyries struggling to generate consistent offense. Golden State’s 64 points marked the lowest total by a team that won a WNBA Finals game since 2005. LESS THAN 2 YEARS AFTER COACHING COLLEGE HOOPS IN FLORIDA, KARL SMESKO LEADS ATLANTA DREAM TO WNBA FINALS Fox News Digital and OutKick contacted the WNBA for comment and asked whether Smesko or Reese could face fines for their remarks about the officiating. Players and coaches have recently been disciplined for criticizing referees. During last year’s playoffs, Las Vegas Aces coach Becky Hammon and Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White were each fined $1,000 during the semifinals after making comments critical of the officiating. Hammon’s and White’s comments came in support of Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve, whose own words about the officiating prompted the league to issue her a one-game suspension. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Game 6 of the 2026 WNBA Finals is scheduled for Thursday at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. The game will tip off at 12:30 p.m. ET after the NBA, WNBA, Atlanta Hawks, Dream and arena reached an agreement to accommodate both teams and avoid disrupting the Hawks’ game later that night. "I hope everyone gets to see it somehow and I know for some people it's not realistic -- they have jobs and won't be able to make it," Smesko said. "I'm disappointed for that, but I'm hopeful as many people can see the game as possible."

articles.title: WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Halloween Havoc 2026
articles.summary: From the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida, NXT presented its final show before Halloween Havoc.
articles.body:
From the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida, NXT presented its final show before Halloween Havoc.

The Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic continued with the two semifinal battles: The Vanity Project vs. Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno and The Wagner Brothers vs. Hank Walker and Tank Ledger. Who would advance to the finals?

Jackson Drake defended his North American Championship against EK Prosper as potential future challengers Saquon Shugars and Sean Legacy collided. Lizzy Rain battled Chantel Monroe.

For all the highlights, results, winners and live grades, scroll down.

Dusty Classic: The Vanity Project vs. Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno

Last Time in Action: Brad Baylor and Ricky Smokes defeated Chazz "Starboy" Hall and Mini Vikingo, and Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno defeated Fraxiom to advance to the semifinals of the Dusty Classic (NXT, October 13).

The Vanity Project went right after Dar, trying to go after his already injured head, including sending him into the same steel steps that broke him open at a live event.

Romeo stepped up and protected The Scottish Supernova by dumping out Baylor onto Smokes. He went to the Picture-in-Picture break as the referee checked on the injured Dar.

Vanity Project continued to isolate Romeo until Dar forced his way into the action, striking hard and fast against Baylor and Smokes.

He caught Baylor in an Armbar that almost forced a submission. After Baylor fought out, Smokes cheap-shot The Scottish Supernova with a Spear to set up a near-fall.

Romeo and Dar locked in Ankle Locks. Vanity Project fought out but accidentally knocked into one another.

As Romeo and Dar set up the finish, they also knocked into one another, setting up Dar for Hit It and Quit It. Romeo broke up the pin attempt.

Dar locked Smokes in the Champagne Superkneebar, but Smokes rolled outside. Myka Lockwood tried to Clothesline Dar, but he ducked it.

Romeo sent Smokes into Baylor on a Hit It and Quit It attempt followed by a High Low Combination to Smokes for the victory.

This was a long, competitive battle that could have gone either way, and NXT went with the more exciting option by giving the win to the underdog team.

With their victory, Romeo and Dar should be the next one ups to face The Vanity Project for the NXT Tag Team Championships regardless of whether they win the Dusty Classic.

However, it feels right for the two to win it all as they have consistently delivered in the ring throughout this tournament, coming as the best team in the company.

They did not click with Baylor and Smokes like Fraxiom, but this was one of the better recent performances from Vanity Project against any team.

It is a shame that the Dusty Classic will not be represented at Halloween Havoc as it is the most effective part of NXT in these last few weeks.

Romeo and Dar def. Smokes and Baylor to advance to the finals of the Dusty Classic.

Dar came in with his head taped up due to recent staples he received after a live event match against The Vanity Project.'

Booker T repeatedly stated that The Scottish Warrior should not be competing with his injury and should have forfeited the tournament.

Vic Joseph announced that the finals of the Dusty Classic would be next week on a Wednesday edition of NXT.

During the match, NXT showed a video where Grayson Waller revealed he was outside Tony D'Angelo's home.

After the match, Tony D told Robert Stone he was heading to his home, threatening to rip Waller's throat out.

Last Time in Action: Lizzy Rain and Chantel Monroe lost in the NXT Women's Championship #1 Contender Battle Royal won by Wren Sinclair (NXT, October 6).

Chantel tried to set the pace against Lizzy, but she quickly found herself overwhelmed by the strikes of The Maiden of Metal.

Lizzy caught her with a Springboard Elbow and a Fisherman Suplex, but Chantel caught her in the ropes with a Hangman Neckbreaker into the commercial break.

A Swinging Neckbreaker into a Running Knee kept Monroe in control out of the break. Lizzy kept Chantel on her toes as she fired back including Machine Gun Chops in the corner and a strong Spinebuster.

Chantel reversed a Backslide into a pin of her own and grabbed the ropes to steal the pinfall.

Lizzy has not done nearly enough in NXT to already be working the veteran role, taking the surprise pin to an obviously inexperienced opponent.

Even if NXT sees big things in Chantel, she was only fine in this match while NXT has yet to capitalize on the popularity and obvious experience edge of The Maiden of Metal.

These two will fight again, and Chantel will need to figure out how to improve her character work and speed in the ring to make this a real feud.

This was the singles debut of Chantel in NXT, and she did not get an entrance.

Booker T called out a lazy pin from Chantel, leading to Vic Joseph repeatedly questioning if Chantel was taking this too lightly.

In a pre-tape, Cruz Montana delivered a warning to Dion Lennox that he would pay for bringing the darkest part of himself out.

Last Time in Action: Saquon Shugars lost to Tristan Angels (NXT, October 13); Sean Legacy alongside EK Prosper and Zilla Fatu lost to BirthRight (NXT, September 22).

Shugars came into this match angry, knocking the camera out of his way. However, the athleticism of Legacy knocked him down early as the match went to an early commercial break.

During the break, Shugars tripped Legacy off the ropes to take over. He kept control back from break by grinding Legacy into the mat.

Legacy struck his way free, landing a strong Superkick to turn the tide. Shugars caught Legacy with an F12 but did not hook both legs, allowing Legacy to get his free leg on the bottom rope.

Legacy landed a Spanish Fly to seal the victory over Shugars, who looked to be in shock afterward.

This was a solid match, though these two are still figuring out their chemistry. This was too often two athletes doing their work rather than a cohesive contest.

Few men have done more with limited time than Legacy, who looks great every time he performs. He is an unreal athlete with impressive body control.

That said, this may have been more about Shugars than Legacy, who heavily played up the idea that he was trying too hard to look cool rather than win.

This ended up costing him the match, which could be the character hook that will help Shugars finally start to put it together in NXT.

While he is one of the most charismatic men in all of NXT, Shugars has yet to figure out what is going to make him a star.

He was a side character in DarkState and did not come out of his DarkState break-up with much hype. Legacy could help Shugars find his focus.

Meanwhile, Shugars could help Legacy establish himself as more than just a fun athlete.

Vic Joseph called Shugars "more flash than substance" due to his focus on playing to the crowd.

Booker T revealed he was focusing even more on pinfall attempts tonight due to William Regal's Tweet from earlier in the month.

In a pre-tape, Izzi Dame explained that she saw through Zaria's facade and exposed a scared girl hiding from who she really is.

Myles Borne and Tavion Heights Find Out They Will Fight in Weapons Wild

Myles Borne and Tavion Heights exchanged final words with security keeping them apart.

Myles said that Tavion was holding him back from his potential while Heights called out Myles as selfish. Both promised to bring their best fight to Halloween Havoc before almost testing security.

Afterward, Danhausen demanded his people spin the Halloween Havoc wheel, revealing the match would be Weapons Wild.

Neither Myles or Tavion are the best promos, but this was heated and focused enough to work.

Both sold why they are a threat to win at Halloween Havoc and what will drive them to succeed.

While NXT is trying to make multiple matches feel heated between Halloween Havoc and next week's NXT, this is clearly the best built feud on paper into the premium live event.

Tony D'Angelo headed home where Grayson Waller called him, telling him he had already left for "the restaurant", so Tony D went back on the hunt.

When D'Angelo found the restaurant, Waller had left him a note to meet "where it all started".

In a pre-tape, Kam Hendrix questioned why he was on the sidelines while EK Prosper was getting a North American Championship match.

Backstage, Robert Stone told Dion Lennox that his match with Cruz Montana next week would be Unsanctioned.

Dusty Classic: The Wagner Brother vs. Hank Walker and Tank Ledger

Last Time in Action: El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno defeated Charlie Dempsey and Lexis King, and Hank Walker and Tank Ledger defeated The Creed Brothers to advance to the semifinals of the Dusty Classic (NXT, October 20).

While Hank and Tank tried to start the pace fast, Wagner and Galeno pushed them to go even faster, utilizing Galeno's size and Wagner's speed to overwhelm the former NXT tag champions.

Into the commercial break, Galeno tossed Wagner onto Hank and Tank on the outside of the ring.

Back from break, Galeno rolled over Hank and Tank Body Slamming them onto one another followed by a Running Splash for two.

Wagner then blasted Hank with a Tope Suicida while Galeno caught Tank with a Running Splash off the apron.

A Galeno Frog Splash on Hank nearly took the victory, but Tank broke up the pin. Both teams met in the center of the ring, and Hank and Tank hit repeating running strikes to lay out Galeno.

Hank caught Wagner with a Boss Man Slam then Hank and Tank hit Galeno with Running Tackles followed by a pair of Diving Splashes for the victory.

This started strong, but the action grew sloppier with time. While The Wagner Brothers were looking to deliver as much action as possible, Hank and Tank struggled to follow.

By the time the dust settled, it did not feel like Hank and Tank had earned the win, and the limited Performance Center crowd did not know how to react.

This is not the way an underdog win should feel, and it seems like NXT might have misjudged how fans would react to this match.

Romeo Moreno and Noam Dar had a strong clear path to the finals, including beating the heel NXT tag champs. It feels like Hank and Tank stumbled to the same spot.

Still, the final is likely to be great given the usual work of both teams in the ring, and both would make sense to emerge the victors since these are explosive teams that could be next up for Vanity Project.

Hank and Tank def. Galeno and Wagner by pinfall to advance to the finals of the Dusty Classic.

During their entrance, The Wagner Brothers found their father Dr. Wagner Jr. in the audience. Cameras caught his reactions throughout.

Booker T questioned how embarrassed The Wagner Brothers would be to lose in front of their father. That question was left open ended after the loss.

NXT showed footage of Kelani Jordan and Iyo Sky arguing on Raw in Adam Pearce's office. Kendal Grey and Wren Sinclair then talked in the locker room where Wren promised to win for the WrenQCC.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream owners say they raised WNBA Finals scheduling conflicts months ago in blistering open letter
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream owners say the WNBA ignored early warnings about State Farm Arena scheduling conflicts, forcing a midday Thursday tip-off for Game 6 of the Finals.
articles.body: The Atlanta Dream raised concerns about scheduling conflicts between the WNBA Finals and other events at the city’s State Farm Arena months ago, according to a blistering open letter to Atlanta released Tuesday night. In the letter addressed to the city of Atlanta, the Dream responded to criticism leveled at the team, the WNBA and the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks over scheduling conflicts that have complicated the WNBA Finals. Games 3 and 4 had to be rescheduled – Game 3 was played a day earlier than originally planned and Game 4 tipped off in the early afternoon instead of evening – due to conflicts with a concert and the Hawks’ home opener. Now that the series is headed to a Game 6, the Dream’s showdown against the Golden State Valkyries will take place at 12:30 p.m. ET Thursday at State Farm Arena because the Hawks host the Cleveland Cavaliers that evening. The issues were known to the Dream and brought to the league’s attention, but the letter signed by owners Larry and Robyn Gottesdiener, Suzanne Abair and Renee Montgomery stated their concerns were largely ignored. “Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena,” the letter read. “As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns. Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved.” “Perhaps it was assumed that the Dream would not make it this far. Perhaps, our place in the Finals was not accounted for. Whatever the reason, the reality is that we are here. We earned our place in the Finals, and our city deserves the opportunity to show up for its team.” The letter added that the 12:30 p.m. ET tip off for Game 6 is “not what we would have chosen and not what we fought for.” The Valkyries hold a 3-2 lead in the Finals and could clinch their first title on Thursday. CNN has reached out to the WNBA for comment on the letter. The Dream, who joined the WNBA as an expansion team in 2008, used State Farm Arena – then known as Philips Arena – for home games from 2008-2016. The Gateway Center Arena, located outside the city in College Park, has served as the team’s full-time home venue for the last six years. The team will move back to State Farm Arena permanently in 2027. The capacity difference between the two arenas is stark: Gateway Center holds roughly 3,500 fans, whereas State Farm seats more than 17,000. Not all WNBA franchises in cities with NBA teams share ownership or arena management. That is the case in Atlanta: the Dream franchise is owned separately from the Hawks, who operate State Farm Arena. The Dream’s owners thanked the Hawks for working to ensure the Finals the games could take place at State Farm Arena. “We believed that our fans and the city wanted the opportunity to be a part of this historic series, and to see it played on a world-class stage. That meant State Farm Arena,” the letter stated. “We are grateful to everyone who helped make that possible, especially our partners - the Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena - who stepped up by adjusting their schedule on the fly, not once, but three times. And what a celebration it has been: a party, a concert and incredible Dream basketball all rolled into one.” The letter added: “That is what Atlanta supporting Atlanta looks like. The Hawks and the Dream are different teams with different histories, but we share a city, a community, and a responsibility to help Atlanta shine on the biggest stages. When one of us has an opportunity to make history, we all want to see it happen.” While NBA evens often take precedence if there’s a double-bookings occur at shared arenas - such as in 2023, when a Janet Jackson concert was postponed to accomodate a first-round Hawks playoff game against the Boston Celtics – the WNBA has a history of playoff games being displaced due to venue availability across its 30 seasons. Just last year, the Valkyries – shocking the WNBA world by reaching the playoffs in their inaugural season in 2025 – moved a first-round playoff game more than 40 miles away to SAP Center in San Jose, the home of the NHL’s San Jose Sharks, because the Laver Cup tennis tournament was booked at Chase Center. CNN’s Jill Martin contributed to this report.

articles.title: McKeel's Swinburne back on track as he wins twice at district swim meet
articles.summary: Bryce Palmer and Claire Scarborough joined Chance Swinburne as two-time individual winners at 2A-7 district swim meet Tuesday.
articles.body:
WAUCHULA — It hasn't exactly been a senior season that McKeel's Chance Swinburne expected.

"I've been sick for most of the season, so it kind of took it away from me of wanting to continue," he said.

Yet as the season winds down and he's begun to feel better, he's starting to feel better about competing. Although he said he's not going to swim competitively after high school, he's hoping to cap his career with his best performances at the state meet.

The road to state began on Tuesday, Oct. 27 as he had little trouble winning his two individual events to help lead the McKeel boys to runner-up finish behind host Hardee in the Class 2A, District 7 Swimming and Diving Meet at the Hardee Recreational Complex.

For the girls, Bryce Palmer and Claire Swinburne each won two individual events, and Elin Jonsson and Jocelyn Chanthavongsa each won one individual event to help lead the girls to the team district title.

As the only individual winner for the boys, Swinburne won the 200-yard freestyle in 1:50.83, then later won the 100 freestyle in 49.14. He was the only swimmer to go sub-50 in the event.

Swinburne said he was happy with his times as he wasn't pushing for fast times. In each race, Swinburne had a slight lead in the first half of the race before pulling away for decisive wins.

"I'm not trying to go for anything here," he said. "I already know I'm making regionals. I've had a weird practice schedule, but it's not really swimming. Like last week, Friday and Saturday, they (club) have practices, so I've been to this meet with one day. I'm not expecting much of it."

Swinburne changed clubs in the past year and now goes to Winter Garden for club practice.

"I've been training with all these people, and I don't get to race them at all," he said. "There are not a lot of people that I can compete with (during the season). Hardee is kind of like the only (team) that I can find someone to compete against, because Marcos Cabrera and I don't swim the same events."

McKeel coach Roy Wilshire said he has seen some improvement in Swinburne's performance recently and said he's in a good spot if he can stay healthy over the next couple of weeks.

"He's got the right mindset," he said. "He knows kind of where his ceiling is there with just a couple of meets left. I'm hopeful he'll maybe reconsider (about not swimming competitively) as he gets beyond the season, but for right now, his focus is these next couple of weeks; get through regionals and get to state and do his best and represent the team, himself, his family."

Last season, Swinburne competed in the 50 free and the 100 free in the postseason. He finished 18th in the preliminaries in the 50 free and did not qualify for the finals. In the 100 free, however, he finished 12th in the preliminaries and 12th in the overall finals. His best time this year of 47.76 would have placed him in the top eight.

Swinburne was the top boys swimmer for McKeel. Luke Durden was second in the 200 IM and the 100 fly, and Brandon Sadler was second in the 50 free.

Palmer, Scarborough shine for McKeel girls

In the girls competition, Bryce Palmer won the 100 butterfly in 1:01.72, and teammate Sophia Silveira Lima was second in 1:04.43. Palmer then won the 100 breaststroke in 1:07.99.

Jonsson faltered early when she finished second in the 200 free but came back strong to win the 100 back in 1:06.21. Chanthavongsa won the 500 free then finished second in the 100 breast.

The McKeel girls also won all three relays.

On Monday, McKeel junior Lyla Paterson won girls diving but didn't finish with enough points to advance to regionals. Riley Pannone was second.

Overall, Wilshire was pleased with how both his girls and boys swimmers did.

"The objective was to get qualified for regionals, make sure if you were positioned in those auto advanced spots, to get through and I think we absolutely met that requirement today," he said. "We didn't necessarily swim great times, but I think collectively, I didn't really see that against with any team for the most part. So I think they did what they were supposed to do."

Lake Wales senior Marcos Cabrera had little trouble advancing in his two events. After opting to again swim in the 50 free in the postseason like last year rather than the 200 individual medley as his second event, Cabrera won the event by nearly two seconds. He finished in 22.10, and McKeel senior Brandon Sadler was second in 23.88.

In his best event, Cabrera won the 100 breaststroke in 58.37. He was the only competitor in the event to finish under one minute.

Lake Wales' Ady Warrick finished second in the 100 back and third in the 200 breast as the Highlanders finished third in the team competition.

articles.title: George Russell F1 title chances defended by Toto Wolff after Helmut Marko comments
articles.summary: Mercedes team chief Toto Wolff has defended George Russell's Formula 1 title prospects
articles.body:
Mercedes Formula 1 team chief Toto Wolff has rejected former Red Bull motorsport adviser Helmut Marko's claim that George Russell will never get another shot at the F1 title.

Russell currently sits 123 points behind his team-mate and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli in the drivers' standings.

While speaking to Sky Sports Deutschland ahead of the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas, Marko said Antonelli had taken over as the Brackley outfit's lead driver.

"Russell is no longer the number one driver. Antonelli has quite clearly taken that spot from him. But Russell is one of the top drivers," Marko said. "I doubt whether he'll ever have another chance at the world title or be given number one status anywhere."

Asked about the comments after the race in Austin, Wolff said Marko had got it wrong.

"I start with Helmut, I mean, he's my Austrian, not-so-buddy, but I respect his opinion. But I think he's wrong on George. George has all the ability. I think the car doesn't suit him."

He added: "I think that at the beginning of the season, it is maybe difficult to cope with the situation where you're feeling that this is my year to come, and then we have this wonderkid on the other side that starts to really chip away. And I believe that a new season, George, if we provide him with a quick car, is absolutely possible.

"He has absolutely what it needs to win a championship. So I think it's a bit too easy to say, let's forget about all these years where he won in F2 and F3, his rookie years and the European championships back-to-back in karting, that's still all there."

The 19th round of the 2026 season, the Mexican Grand Prix, is scheduled for 30 October to 1 November.

articles.summary: Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer dismissed a cornerback from the team after he was arrested leading up to the Crimson Tide game against Texas A&M. The post Al...
articles.body:
Alabama is on its bye week, but drama surrounds the team. Right before the Crimson Tide's 31-20 win over Texas A&M on Saturday, Alabama suspended defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. for violating team rules. Alabama suspended him, but it didn't give a specific reason. That changed on Monday.

Nick Kelly and Carol Robinson from Alabama.com reported on Monday that Kirkpatrick was arrested Friday on two misdemeanor charges.

"Alabama defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. was arrested Friday on two misdemeanor charges, per court documents obtained by AL.com on Monday," Kelly and Robinson wrote.

Kirkpatrick was charged with harassing communications and doxing. Head coach Kalen DeBoer dismissed Kirkpatrick from the team on Tuesday.

"After gathering more information on the situation, Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. will no longer be a part of our program," DeBoer said in a statement via On3's Nick Schultz. "He did not live up to the standards and expectations that I have set for this team and our players."

ESPN's Alex Scarborough reported on Monday that Kirkpatrick is facing misdemeanor charges related to allegedly threatening communications with a police officer involved in his arrest in 2025.

"The veteran defensive back allegedly sent the officer a profanity-laced message that included, 'text me back don't be no b—-!,' according to documents obtained by WBRC and The Tuscaloosa Thread, Scarborough wrote. Kirkpatrick allegedly posted a photo of the officer and his family to his Facebook page with the caption, "Dis him?"

Kirkpatrick was arrested last year on three counts of reckless endangerment and one count of attempting to elude and speeding. Alabama suspended him for the rest of the 2025 season after his arrest.

Kirkpatrick joined the Alabama football team in 2024, appeared in 28 games, and this season appeared in seven games, recording five combined tackles.

Many Alabama fans knew the name Kirkpatrick before he arrived on campus because his dad, Dre Kirkpatrick, played for the Crimson Tide from 2009 to 2011 and won two national titles.

articles.title: Anaheim Ducks Confirm Goaltender Decision Ahead of Canucks Game
articles.summary: The Anaheim Ducks have announced their starting goaltender for their Tuesday night matchup vs. the Vancouver Canucks.Daily Faceoff and Derek Lee have confirm...
articles.body:
The Anaheim Ducks have announced their starting goaltender for their Tuesday night matchup vs. the Vancouver Canucks.

Daily Faceoff and Derek Lee have confirmed that Lukas Dostal will man the crease for the Ducks. Dostal is 4-4-0 this season with an .880 save percentage, a 3.27 GAA, and zero shutouts.

Despite posting some rough numbers to start the season, Dostal could be in for a good game on Tuesday. The Canucks have been the worst team in hockey since their 17-goal outburst in their first three games of the season.

Vancouver split their season-opening home-and-home series against the Edmonton Oilers. They started the season 2-1 following a 4-1 victory over the Calgary Flames. But they have since fallen back to reality. The Canucks are 0-9-1 in their last 10 matchups with 20 goals scored, so this is Dostal's game to lose.

The pressure won't just be on Dostal, however. If the Ducks wish to ensure they don't have a trap game on their hands, it will take a full effort from all over the lineup.

Anaheim Ducks Projected Lines And Pairings vs. Vancouver

Patrick Present shared the line combos and pairings for Tuesday's matchup, and Cutter Gauthier, Leo Carlsson, and Judd Caulfield look like the top trio. Caulfield has seen action in nine games and has four points and 26 hits this year.

Jeff Malott, Mikael Granlund, and Beckett Sennecke are the projected second line. Sennecke will look to keep up his over half-goal-per-game pace, with six in 11 games (nine points).

The projected third line looks like Nikita Nesterenko, Roger McQueen, and Alex Killorn. Killorn would be the seasoned veteran of the group should the projection hold, and he has five points in 11 contests.

Tim Washe is slated to center A.J. Greer and Sam Colangelo on the fourth line. Washe currently has six points in 11 games and has landed 39 body checks this season.

Jackson LaCombe and Noah Warren are the projected first pairing for Tuesday night. LaCombe is creeping toward the point-per-game mark with nine in 11 contests.

Tyson Hinds and Tristan Luneau make up the projected second pairing. Luneau is looking to stay consistent after his recent outburst in points .

Finally, Travis Mitchell and Nick Jensen project for the third pairing. Jensen has six blocks in two games this season.

Ducks Should Be Well-Rested And Have Momentum On Their Side

Like Vancouver, the Anaheim Ducks faced a losing streak of their own after starting the season 4-1-0. Luckily for Anaheim, they got the best of the Philadelphia Flyers on Oct. 24, and they scored five times in the process. If the Ducks emulate that on Tuesday night, they should skate away with the win.

That said, Dostal didn't have his best outing against Philadelphia. He allowed four goals on 32 shots, good for just an .875 save percentage. Philadelphia hasn't exactly been all-world in the offensive zone, so Dostal must bounce back vs. Vancouver.

If Anaheim gets the win, they will be back at .500 and could be on the verge of another solid string of games. But they must prove they can beat teams they're supposed to beat, and not play down to their competition. The Ducks will get that chance when the puck drops at 10:00 p.m. EDT.

articles.title: High school cross country: Viewmont girls celebrates first-ever 5A state title, Maple Mountain boys repeat
articles.summary: High school cross country: Viewmont girls celebrates first-ever 5A state title, Maple Mountain boys repeat
articles.body:
Five years removed from not even qualifying for the 5A state meet, Viewmont's girls cross country team turned in a tremendous performance during Tuesday's state meet at Sugar House Park to capture its first state championship in school history.

Not only did the Vikings overcome their own bleak history in winning, but also their own disappointment from just a couple weeks ago when they finished third in the Region 6 meet behind Brighton and Olympus.

Viewmont coach Trent Hooper helped his girls refocus with a better mindset for state, and they stormed forward to win that elusive title.

"We focused on that practice after practice and at Divisionals, and they just executed it on a big stage today," said Hooper, who took over as Viewmont's head coach in 2022 after the school missed out on back-to-back state meets the two years prior.

Success didn't come overnight after Hooper was hired, it took a patient approach to change the culture and establish tradition, but mission accomplished for the entire Vikings program after Tuesday's big victory.

Viewmont had its top five runners place in the top 23 as it tallied 83 points to finish narrowly ahead of the same Olympus team it finished behind at region. The Titans tallied 93 points, followed by defending state champion Springville with 128 points.

Senior Lydia Stringfellow was the lone Viewmont runner who finished inside the top 10 as she finished in seventh place.

While Viewmont's girls were busy celebrating their first-ever title, Maple Mountain's boys won its second straight 5A state championship and third in the past four years.

The Golden Eagles ran away with the title with 71 team points, with Viewmont in second with 120 points. Patience was the key for Maple Mountain coach Brett Andrus.

He stressed to his athletes all season, and particularly ahead of the state meet, to stay patient in the first mile. Sure enough, at the first mile marker, Maple Mountain sat in third position as a team.

That was exactly where Andrus expected and hoped his team would be. It was their performance after that first mile that separated his team from the 5A field.

"We have worked on knowing that when we got here, that we would be very patient in that first mile, and then we would let our strength carry us the last half of the race. They followed through with that race plan," said Andrus.

While Andrus said no question having Logan Rohatinsky and Parker Davis finish second and third overall was massive for team scoring, he couldn't stop raving about how well his No. 3, 4 and 5 runners executed the race plan.

Landon Smith went from 21st place to 11th place after the first mile. Andrew Olsen went from 50th to 25th and then senior Asher Gunderson went from 67th to 30th in his first-ever race at the state meet.

"Those are the things that we want to see on a course like this. That means that we're learning how to run this course the way that we run it year in and year out, even if we have to replace people," said Andrus, who reiterated that Gunderson's success was one of the brightest moments of the day.

Northridge's Jeff Hazard claimed the 5A boys individual state title has he pulled away from Rohatinsky in the final 400 meters to avenge last year's state runner-up finish to Rohatinsky.

Hazard has been dealing with Achilles tendinitis this season, but it wasn't a factor on Tuesday as he managed the fast pace better than everyone else after West Field's Daxton Coombs went out very fast to start the race.

"I'm just so happy. Even though I knew it was possible, I was shocked coming across the line and just was so excited. It was awesome," said Hazard, who won the title with a time of 15:06.53, with Rohatinsky in second with a time of 15:14.62.

Hazard finished second to Rohatinsky by 17 seconds at the 5A Divisional meet a few weeks ago, but said his race strategy at the state meet set himself up much better for success

While Rohatinsky's bid for a 5A repeat came up a bit short, his little sister made a sparkling debut in her first-ever state tournament.

The freshman pulled away from Brighton junior Bridget Smit in the final mile to win with a time of 17:53.56. Smith crossed the line in 17:56.74.

Rohatinsky has been a regular attendee at state meets in recent years watching her older siblings compete, but she said running inside the ropes this time around was a surreal experience.

"I was so excited. I feel like the nerves like hit me like before the race, but I feel like they were more excitement nerves than nervous nerves, which I feel like that was a big advantage," said Rohatinsky. "And then to be in the course, it's just a lot different than cheering for my brothers, and it was just like a special experience."

Rohatinsky's dad Josh Rohatinsky is one of the most decorated runners in Utah state history as he won four individual cross country state championships at Provo from 1996 to 1999. All of his wins came on a very similar course at Sugar House Park.

By winning her debut state meet this week, the kickoff to Oaklie Rohatisnky's career got off to a smashing start.

articles.title: Longtime Nebraska play-by-play announcer Kent Pavelka will retire following 2026-2027 season
articles.summary: One of the most legendary voices of Nebraska men’s basketball and football is hanging up the headset. Longtime play-by-play announcer Kent Pavelka, who began...
articles.body:
One of the most legendary voices of Nebraska men's basketball and football is hanging up the headset.

Longtime play-by-play announcer Kent Pavelka, who began calling Cornhusker games in 1974, announced Monday evening on Huskers Radio Network that he will retire after the 2026-27 season, per the Daily Nebraskan .

"It's time," Pavelka said on the radio show. "It takes just about everything deep in my soul to share that. There comes a time, a lot of friends and family know.

"What I intend to do is enjoy this last go-around and savor it. As we make our way around the country, I'll be smiling inside and celebrating inside all the memories. We're gonna focus on this basketball team and its quest. Here's what I'm dreaming of: that they get into the third week of March this year, when all is said and done.

"The point is, I never wanted to do anything else — just this. What we're going to do now is focus on this game tonight and these Huskers and the story they create over the next four or five months."

Pavelka's Husker radio career began at KFAB, where he did football color commentary from 1974 through 1983 before becoming the play-by-play voice from 1984 through 1996. He also became the play-by-play announcer for Nebraska men's basketball in 1974 and initially held that role until 1996. He returned in 2006 to call men's basketball, a role he still enjoys today . Pavelka was inducted into the Nebraska Broadcasters Association Hall of Fame in 2019.

"We look forward to properly saluting Kent later this season in honor of his lifetime of passion passed through the airwaves to generations of Husker faithful," wrote Nebraska AD Troy Dannen on X .

articles.title: Dabo Swinney struggling with Clemson, excelling in fantasy football
articles.summary: Despite Clemson’s struggles on the field, Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney is finding success in fantasy football.
articles.body:
Dabo Swinney's family finally gave him a spot in its fantasy football league this season. Now, the Clemson head coach has some bragging rights over the relatives who questioned whether he knew enough to compete.

Swinney shared the update during Tuesday's press conference ahead of the Tigers ' trip to Florida State , offering a lighter moment as the Tigers prepare to respond to their loss to Virginia Tech.

"It's like my big Swinney family [league], and they wouldn't let me in it," Swinney said. "It's the first year they've let me be in it, you know, and I'm like, well, why can't I be in it? Well, 'You don't really know what you're doing.' They finally let me in it."

His debut has worked out well enough to inspire a joke about a possible career change.

"Maybe I should retire and be a full-time fantasy guy," Swinney said.

One player helping fuel that confidence is Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Tre Tucker. Swinney acknowledged that familiarity with the receiver had little to do with his decision to draft him, but he has enjoyed the results.

"I made a great draft pickup," Swinney said. "I got some guy named Tucker from the Raiders. He is killing it. He's making hay every week. I didn't know who he was."

Clemson 's actual season has provided fewer reasons to celebrate. Saturday's 20-16 loss dropped the Tigers to 4-3 overall and 2-2 in ACC play heading into the Florida State matchup.

Within the family competition, though, Swinney is enjoying his place in the standings.

"Yeah, I'm in first place in the league," he said. "So, my fantasy life's pretty good."

articles.title: UConn humbles Purdue basketball in final exhibition tune up
articles.summary: Purdue led briefly at UConn before the Huskies turned it on and held Purdue to a cold shooting first half.
articles.body:
The exhibition slate of games concluded with a harsh and humbling regular season tune-up for Purdue basketball .

The No. 24 Boilermakers suffered early shooting and turnover woes and found themselves chasing from a double digit deficit quickly against one of the nation's top programs.

Fifth-ranked UConn coasted past Purdue 76-53 at PeoplesBank Arena.

It's the fourth straight season the Boilers lost a road exhibition game against a power conference program, including Arkansas in 2023, Creighton in 2024 and Kentucky last season.

Purdue now turns its attention to its regular season opener against Gonzaga in Las Vegas on Nov. 2.

Photos from last Tuesday's Purdue basketball open practice.

Purdue basketball turning point vs UConn

The Boilermakers made just 5-of-21 shots to open the game and it wasn't until Raleigh Burgess rebounded his own miss and kicked to Jack Benter for an open 3 with 2:25 to go in the first half that Purdue made a shot from beyond the arc.

The Boilermakers, who trailed 17-7 midway through the first half, finished the opening 20 minutes just 1-of-14 from 3. The Boilers finished 2-of-25 from deep.

By halftime, UConn led 35-20 and held Purdue to 26.7% shooting. The Boilermakers couldn't recover from the early hole. Purdue had a chance to cut the lead to seven early in the second half but Omer Mayer's open corner 3 caromed off the rim, leading to a conventional three-point play for UConn's Silas Demary Jr.

Jayden Ross set the tone early for the Huskies. He was 4-for-4, including 3-for-3 with 11 points in the opening half. Ross finished with 13 points, 2 rebounds and 1 assist in 18 minutes.

3 standouts for Purdue basketball vs. UConn

CJ Cox: Cox accounted for half of Purdue's first half offense, scoring 10 points on 4-of-9 shooting. The rest of the team in that stretch was 4-for-21. Cox finished with a game high 18 points on 50% shooting and also had 6 rebounds.

Caden Pierce: For the Boilermakers to have success this season, they'll need solid rebounding from the former Ivy League Player of the Year. Purdue was outmatched Tuesday on the glass but held its own. Pierce supplying 7 boards (4 offensive) helped in that regard.

Daniel Jacobsen: The 7-foot-4 center is not a finished product but he's definitely showing his game changer ability with his length. Jacobsen blocked four shots and totaled 10 in three exhibition games. When he gets to his spot in the post, he's hard to stop. Jacobsen finished with 7 points, 4 rebounds and an assist.

Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking.

articles.title: 3 things that stood out from Purdue basketball's blowout exhibition loss at UConn
articles.summary: The Boilermakers did not shoot it well, and it led to playing from behind. Here's what we learned in the preseason finale.
articles.body:
HARTFORD, CT — Purdue basketball received the challenge it wanted from UConn in its final exhibition and then some, falling 76-53 at PeoplesBank Arena on Tuesday.

The Boilermakers remained winless in their recent run of exhibition road games against high-major opponents. C.J. Cox scored 18 points, but functional offense was hard to come by for much of the night.

Purdue basketball photos vs. UConn in college basketball action

Purdue couldn't make a 3, couldn't muster enough functional offense elsewhere

Matt Painter wanted to play UConn for the simple reason the Huskies "run good offense and make it hard for you to run good offense." He probably wasn't expecting a 1-for-14 first-half shooting performance from 3, a handful of missed opportunities inside and a generally flat offensive performance. (That one made 3 came when Raleigh Burgess whiffed a layup but got the ball back and found Jack Benter behind the line.)

Purdue does not need to be explosive on offense this season, but it must be efficient. Instead, it looked off-kilter for much of the first half. Between those missed 3s and turnovers it had 18 empty offensive possessions in the first half alone. It finished 2_-25 from 3, which probably won't happen often. The inability to create fast break chances or finish around the rim may actually be bigger concerns.

Purdue received a final rebounding reminder before season's start

UConn projected as a much more significant rebounding challenge, and delivered. Three of the Huskies' offensive rebounds came on one possession which did not yield points, but in general, Purdue had a harder time rewarding itself for stops than in the first two exhibitions. UConn also set a tone with the way it attacked off defensive rebounds, beating the Boilers down the floor for a couple of 3s and a run-out dunk in the first eight minutes of the game.

When Purdue flipped the rebounding advantage in the opening minutes of the second half, it started to cut into the lead. It simply couldn't convert enough on offense to ever challenge to take the lead.

Braylon Mullins back on the floor, again facing off with Luke Ertel

Greenfield-Central alum Braylon Mullins made his exhibition debut for UConn after missing the first two with an unspecified injury. He provided some hints as to his affliction, though, wearing braces on both knees. When he subbed out of the game, he immediately went to a stationary bike positioned near the court. Purdue kept the NCAA Tournament hero in check — seven points on 3-9 shooting — but he also distributed four assists in the first half.

He and Purdue freshman Luke Ertel, a Mt. Vernon grad, went head-to-head in some memorable high school games. He scored two points on 1-4 shooting in this Hancock County reunion.
